tool_input.notes: M.G.L. c. 186, § 18 is an anti-retaliation statute. It makes landlords liable for reprisals against tenants who report code violations, pursue legal action or join tenant unions. If a landlord sends a termination notice (other than for nonpayment), a rent increase or a substantial change in terms within six months of protected activity, the law presumes it was a reprisal. It also voids any lease clause that waives these protections. None of this fits the strict categories. It does not list permitted causes for ending or not renewing a tenancy, so it is not just_cause_eviction. It does not cap or set a formula for rent increases, so it is not rent_increase_limits. It does not cover security deposits, application fees, screening criteria or algorithmic rent setting. No rules recorded.
